- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or flat, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days); cap forecast at +3–4 points above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5 points in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 18d average, reduce by 1–2 points; if below, raise by 0.5–1 point.
- For 30d horizon, avoid extreme outliers (±5% of 18d mean); cap forecasts within ±3% of recent 18d range unless sentiment strongly supports deviation.
